Report No.: M20/R/ML/2026/11
22 October 2026

Finance Committee

The responsibilities of this Committee include checking whether the various expenditures made by State offices are made in the manner permitted by law and in accordance with the budget passed by the Majlis, and checking whether the amounts of money approved by the Majlis are being spent or used for that purpose. They also include the Committee examining, where State offices have spent money beyond the approved amount, the reasons and circumstances that required that money to be spent. In this regard, in looking into matters relating to State finances, they include studying the financial accounts of State offices, State-owned companies, State business enterprises and independent State institutions, studying the various reports of the Auditor General, identifying the measures that must be taken and informing the relevant State offices. In addition, they include carrying out the matters required in relation to the role the Majlis must play in the State taking loans and the State giving guarantees, overseeing the work of the Maldives Monetary Authority and the Auditor General's Office, and seeking the advice of other committees in determining the salaries that must be determined by the People's Majlis.

1. Introduction

As stated in number 10 of Article 120(b) of the Rules of Procedure of the People's Majlis, the responsibilities of the Finance Committee include advising the Majlis in determining the salaries and allowances that must be determined by the People's Majlis, and seeking the advice of other relevant committees in determining those salaries. Accordingly, this report is the report of the Committee's study and decision on the matter of reviewing, among the salaries and allowances to be determined by the People's Majlis under Article 102 of the Constitution of the Republic of Maldives, the salary and allowances of the Speaker of the People's Majlis, the vehicle allowances of members of the Cabinet, and the allowances of island councillors. The schedule included in this report is a part of this report.

2. Documents considered by the Committee in studying the matter

In studying this matter, the Committee considered the following reports.

1. The report passed by the People's Majlis on 28 December 2010, "Report on the Finance Committee's fresh review and decision on the matter, following the Majlis sending back to the Committee the report concluded on 26 August 2010 and submitted to the Majlis by the Finance Committee on reviewing/formulating the salary structure to be determined by the People's Majlis under Article 102 of the Constitution and 10 of Article 100(a) of the Rules of Procedure of the People's Majlis";

2. The report passed by the People's Majlis on 31 December 2012, "Report on the Finance Committee's fresh review and decision on the salary structure to be determined by the People's Majlis under Article 102 of the Constitution and 10 of Article 100(a) of the Rules of Procedure of the People's Majlis" (Report No. މލކ/2012/ރ-10);

3. The report passed by the People's Majlis on 21 July 2014, "Amendment proposed to the report concluded on 25 December 2012 by the Finance Committee on its fresh review of the salary structure to be determined by the People's Majlis under Article 102 of the Constitution and 10 of Article 100(a) of the Rules of Procedure of the People's Majlis" (Report No. މލކ/2014/ރ-3); and

[signature]
[stamp]

4. The report passed by the People's Majlis on 28 February 2024, "Report on the review and reformulation of the structure of salaries and allowances to be determined by the People's Majlis" (Report No. M19/ML/2024/01).

3. How the Committee's work proceeded

The Finance Committee of the People's Majlis has noted that there are disparities in the salaries and allowances currently received by those who receive salaries and allowances that must be determined by the People's Majlis under Article 102 of the Constitution of the Republic of Maldives. Therefore, in order to reduce the disparities in the salaries and allowances received by such posts, it was decided by a majority of the members present and voting at the Committee's 24th meeting, held on 21 October 2026, that the Finance Committee would take the initiative to review those salaries and allowances and deliberate on it among the members.

4. How the Committee's deliberations proceeded

At the Committee's 24th meeting, held on 21 October 2026, the members of the Committee deliberated on the following matters.

4.1. Salary and allowances of the Speaker of the People's Majlis

It is noted that the total amount the Speaker of the People's Majlis receives as salary and allowances is less than that of the Deputy Speaker of the People's Majlis and the members of the Majlis. Accordingly, while the Speaker of the People's Majlis currently receives a total of MVR 73,125 (seventy-three thousand one hundred and twenty-five) as salary and allowances, the Deputy Speaker of the People's Majlis currently receives a total of MVR 91,000 (ninety-one thousand) as salary and allowances. And a member of the People's Majlis currently receives a total of MVR 82,500 (eighty-two thousand five hundred) as salary and allowances. Therefore, the Committee decided to review the allowances of the Speaker of the People's Majlis, set MVR 22,000 (twenty-two thousand) as a special allowance, and set a total of MVR 95,125 (ninety-five thousand one hundred and twenty-five) as the salary and allowances of the Speaker of the People's Majlis.

[signature]
[stamp]

With this change, it is estimated that an additional MVR 264,000 (two hundred and sixty-four thousand) per year will be spent on the salary and allowances of the Speaker of the People's Majlis compared to what is currently spent. 4.2. Vehicle allowance of members of the Cabinet

The salaries and allowances of posts whose salaries and allowances must be determined by the People's Majlis have been determined within a framework formulated for that purpose. However, looking at the changes made to the salaries and allowances of those posts at various times, the Committee has noted that posts of a lower grade are receiving a higher salary than the salary received by members of the Cabinet. Accordingly, although the post of a member of the Cabinet is a post of a higher grade than the chief justices, judges, chief qazis and qazis of the courts, and the heads of independent posts and the presidents of independent institutions are posts of the same grade as members of the Cabinet, the salary received by members of the Cabinet

[signature]
[stamp]

the Committee has noted, is less than the salary received by the posts stated above. The Committee has also noted that, compared to the vehicle allowances received by members of the Cabinet, unequal vehicle allowances are being received by others, including the Chief Justice of the Maldives, the judges of the Supreme Court of the Maldives, the heads of independent posts, the presidents of independent institutions and the mayors of city councils. Therefore, the members of the Committee deliberated on reviewing the vehicle allowances of members of the Cabinet. Currently, the vehicle allowances received total MVR 7,500 (seven thousand five hundred), comprising MVR 1,000 (one thousand) as petrol allowance and MVR 6,500 (six thousand five hundred) as drivers' salary. After deliberation in the Committee, the Committee decided to set a total of MVR 17,000 (seventeen thousand) as vehicle allowances, comprising MVR 2,000 (two thousand) as petrol allowance, MVR 12,000 (twelve thousand) as drivers' salary and MVR 3,000 (three thousand) as drivers' living allowance. With this change, it is estimated that an additional MVR 1,710,000 (one million seven hundred and ten thousand) per year will be spent on the vehicle allowances of members of the Cabinet compared to what is currently spent. 4.3. Allowance of island councillors

Looking at the salaries and allowances of city councillors and island councillors elected under the decentralised system, the Committee has noted that there is a relatively large disparity in those salaries and allowances. Accordingly, while the mayor of a city council receives a total of MVR 46,000 (forty-six thousand) as salary and allowances, a deputy mayor receives a total of MVR 40,500 (forty thousand five hundred) as salary and allowances. And members of a city council receive a total of MVR 35,000 (thirty-five thousand) as salary and allowances. However, the president of an island council currently receives only a total of MVR 25,500 (twenty-five thousand five hundred) as salary and allowances. And while the vice president of an island council currently receives a total of MVR 20,000 (twenty thousand) as salary and allowances, the members of an island council currently receive a total of MVR 18,000 (eighteen thousand) as salary and allowances. Looking at the amounts stated above, the Committee has noted that there is a large disparity in the salaries of island council presidents, vice presidents and island council members compared to the salaries of city council mayors, deputy mayors and city council members.

In addition, following the migration of council staff to the State pay framework on 01 November 2025, there has been a positive change in the salaries of council staff. And with this change, it has come to the Committee's attention that the salaries of councillors elected by the people to run the affairs of the people of the islands on democratic principles are lower than the salaries of administrative staff in some posts in the councils. Therefore, the Committee decided to review the salaries and allowances of island council presidents, vice presidents and island council members. Accordingly, the Committee decided to add MVR 5,000 (five thousand) as a service allowance, in addition to the salaries and allowances currently received by island council presidents, vice presidents and island council members. Therefore, with the newly added service allowance, the president of an island council will receive a total of MVR 30,500 (thirty thousand five hundred)

[signature]
[stamp]

as salary and allowances, while the vice president of an island council will receive a total of MVR 25,000 (twenty-five thousand) as salary and allowances. And a member of an island council will receive a total of MVR 23,000 (twenty-three thousand) as salary and allowances. With this change, it is estimated that an additional MVR 37,560,000 (thirty-seven million five hundred and sixty thousand) per year will be spent on councillors' salaries and allowances compared to what is currently spent. 5. The Committee's decision

Regarding the matter taken up on the Committee's own initiative after the Finance Committee of the People's Majlis noted that there are disparities in the salaries and allowances currently received by those who receive salaries that must be determined by the People's Majlis under Article 102 of the Constitution of the Republic of Maldives, after deliberation at the Committee's 24th meeting of 2026, the majority of members present at the Committee decided to set a special allowance for the Speaker of the People's Majlis, to increase the vehicle allowances of members of the Cabinet, to set a service allowance for the presidents, vice presidents and members of island councils, and to pass it with the changes deliberated and reviewed in the Committee.

The proposed date for providing the salaries and allowances with the changes proposed to the salary structure by the People's Majlis is from the day this report is passed on the floor of the People's Majlis.

Therefore, we submit this report to the People's Majlis under 12 of Article 120(b) of the Rules of Procedure of the People's Majlis, for the Majlis to decide on this report.
